thread:
sara_ng: Seeing weird negative tokens/sec on the Console streaming view for route `acme-prod`. Started around 03:00 UTC, intermittent but recurring. Screenshot and sample window below. :eyes:

metrics-bot: ALERT: streaming_tokens_rate (route=acme-prod) dropped below 0 at 2025-07-12T03:12:00Z. alert_id=alert-7123

raj_patel: Can you paste the query you ran to reproduce? which aggregation window?

sara_ng: I used the dashboard raw query (1m window). SQL snippet:```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', ts) AS minute, SUM(tokens_delta) AS tokens_per_min
FROM streaming_metrics
WHERE route = 'acme-prod'
  AND ts >= '2025-07-12T02:50:00Z'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;
```
Sample rows: `2025-07-12T03:10:00Z -> 1800`, `2025-07-12T03:11:00Z -> -1200`, `2025-07-12T03:12:00Z -> -300`, `2025-07-12T03:13:00Z -> 1600`

emily_w: Negative deltas usually mean the counter reset or we’re computing delta incorrectly (not handling monotonic counters). Any recent restarts of the metrics-extractor or runtime?

mike_t: I checked infra events: there was a staged restart of a runtime pod at 03:08 for a minor deploy (pod runtime-acme-03). Logs show a metrics rehydrate sequence around 03:09 where client sent a `cache_clear` event. Could be double-processing of last_seen per host.

raj_patel: Can you grep the ingestion consumer logs for 'counter_reset' or 'last_seen' around that time? Also want the raw Kafka offsets for the streaming_metrics topic.

sara_ng: Grepped logs, found repeated lines:```
[2025-07-12T03:09:12Z] INFO metrics-consumer-2 rehydrate: last_seen=1700123456789 host=runtime-acme-03
[2025-07-12T03:09:12Z] WARN metrics-consumer-2 computed delta -1200 for key=acme-prod|model-v1
```
Kafka offsets: topic streaming_metrics partition 3 offsets 140020..140180 (spike window).

emily_w: That WARN is the issue. Our aggregation assumes counters are monotonic across ingestion boundaries; when a runtime rehydrates and emits a lower absolute counter (due to in-memory reset), delta becomes negative. We used to clamp negatives in legacy pipeline but the streaming rollup service removed the clamp for performance.

mike_t: Quick mitigation: update the dashboard aggregation to use `GREATEST(SUM(tokens_delta), 0)` or change viz to use non-negative clamp. I'll patch the Vega transform on the Console route to hide negatives while we fix pipeline. Any objections? :thinking:

raj_patel: Do it. Also open an infra/ingest ticket to make the consumer apply a monotonicity fix with host-level watermarks. We should also reprocess the small window to correct historical numbers for billing-sensitive views.

sara_ng: Created ticket INF-4827: "streaming rollup: negative tokens from counter rehydrate after runtime restart" and linked to dashboard patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5912

console-bot: PR merged to staging and rollout started to staging-console at 2025-07-12T10:22:00Z. change: clamp streaming tokens viz to non-negative values.

mike_t: For the long-term fix, propose consumer change: when computing delta for a (route, host, model) key, if delta < -threshold (e.g., -10k) treat as reset and use current_value as baseline (i.e., skip negative delta), and emit metric with 0. Will file a follow-up with ingestion team.

emily_w: Agreed. Also add a periodic watermark record from runtime to avoid silent rehydrates.

sara_ng: Applying dashboard patch as stopgap now. Will reprocess the 03:08-03:14 window in staging to validate. If that looks good, schedule prod reprocess overnight.

raj_patel: Thanks — assign eng-runtime and eng-infra. Tagging @mike_t @emily_w for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: INFO: Incident INF-4827 created and assigned to eng-runtime, eng-ingest. Priority: P2.

sara_ng: Update: staging reprocess completed, numbers corrected, negative values gone. Rolling display update to prod at 21:00 UTC pending approval.

mike_t: I'll take prod rollout and run the consumer patch tomorrow. Leaving notes in INF-4827 on rollout steps and reprocess command:```bash
# reprocess small window
consumer-reprocess --topic streaming_metrics --from-offset 140020 --to-offset 140180 --apply-monotonic-clamp
```

sara_ng: Thanks team — closing a temporary support loop. Will monitor Console for a full day then mark resolved. :shipit:
